pending_interview.category: System design (ML/AI-specific) — RAG at scale, eval pipeline design, recommendation systems, agent platforms, feature store design
pending_interview.question: You are asked to design a feature store for a large e-commerce company. A feature store is a centralized system that computes, stores, and serves input signals — called features — that machine learning models need to make predictions (for example, "how many times has this user purchased in the last 7 days"). The company runs dozens of ML models: real-time product recommendation, fraud detection, churn prediction, and search ranking. Each model has different latency requirements: fraud detection must respond in under 20 milliseconds, while churn prediction runs in overnight batch jobs. Walk through your high-level design. How do you handle the fact that some features need to be served in real time and others are fine computed in batch? How do you prevent the same feature logic from being written differently by different teams (causing training/serving skew — where a model trained on one version of a feature gets served a different version in production)? And how does your design scale as the number of models and features grows by 10x?
